subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which micro-organism is deliberately and usefully employed in bread-making?
questions.explain: Yeast is a useful micro-organism that ferments sugars to leaven bread and brew alcohol.

questions.q: Non-starch polysaccharide (dietary fibre) is important in the diet mainly because it:
options: Aids the passage of food through the gut and prevents constipation
Is a high biological value protein
Is the body's main source of essential fatty acids
questions.explain: NSP adds bulk, holds water and promotes peristalsis, helping prevent constipation and bowel disease.

questions.q: Salmonella food poisoning is most commonly associated with:
options: Raw or undercooked poultry and eggs
questions.explain: Salmonella is frequently linked to raw or undercooked poultry, eggs and their products.

questions.q: Adding lemon juice to cut fruit slows enzymic browning because:
options: The acidity inhibits the enzyme activity
questions.explain: The low pH of lemon juice denatures the browning enzymes, slowing the reaction.

questions.q: The Maillard reaction responsible for the brown crust on roast meat is a reaction between:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is non-enzymic browning between amino acids and reducing sugars on heating.

questions.q: Which mineral is most associated with the prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; a deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: A food described as containing high biological value (HBV) protein is one that:
options: Contains no amino acids at all
Contains all the essential amino acids
questions.explain: HBV proteins supply all the indispensable (essential) amino acids the body cannot synthesise.

questions.q: Which type of fatty acid contains no carbon-to-carbon double bonds?
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have all carbon bonds filled with hydrogen and no double bonds.

questions.q: E. coli O157 is a particularly dangerous pathogen because it:
options: Produces a toxin that can cause severe illness and kidney damage from a low dose
Is destroyed instantly at fridge temperatures
questions.explain: E. coli O157 needs only a small infective dose and can cause serious illness including kidney failure.

questions.q: A diet persistently high in saturated fat and salt most strongly increases the risk of:
questions.explain: High saturated fat and salt raise blood cholesterol and pressure, key risk factors for CHD.

questions.q: Which best describes glycogen?
options: A storage polysaccharide of glucose found in the liver and muscles
questions.explain: Glycogen is the body's storage carbohydrate, a branched polymer of glucose units.

questions.q: Vitamin D is important in the diet because it:
options: Acts as an antioxidant in cell membranes
Promotes absorption of calcium and phosphorus
questions.explain: Vitamin D regulates calcium and phosphorus absorption, essential for healthy bones and teeth.

questions.q: 'Food provenance' refers to:
options: The number of calories in a food
The retail price of the food
Where and how food was grown, reared or caught
questions.explain: Provenance concerns the origin and production method of food, increasingly important to consumers.

questions.q: Vacuum packing helps preserve food chiefly by:
options: Removing oxygen so aerobic spoilage organisms cannot grow
Heating the food to sterilise it
Adding sugar to lower water activity
questions.explain: Removing oxygen inhibits aerobic micro-organisms and slows oxidative spoilage of the food.

questions.q: Gelatinisation occurs when:
options: Amino acids react with reducing sugars
Fat and water are mixed with an emulsifier
Starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating, thickening the mixture
Sugar is heated until it browns
questions.explain: On heating in liquid, starch granules absorb water, swell and burst, thickening the sauce.

questions.q: Trans fatty acids in the diet are of particular concern because they:
options: Raise LDL and lower HDL cholesterol
Lower LDL and raise HDL cholesterol
Have no effect on blood cholesterol
questions.explain: Trans fats raise harmful LDL while lowering protective HDL cholesterol, increasing CHD risk.

questions.q: Salting and sugaring preserve foods primarily by:
options: Reducing the water activity available to micro-organisms
questions.explain: High salt or sugar concentrations draw water out by osmosis, lowering aw and inhibiting microbes.

questions.q: For food to be certified halal, the most important requirement is that:
options: It is completely free from carbohydrate
It is only ever served cold
It contains no pork and meat is slaughtered according to Islamic law
questions.explain: Halal food excludes pork and requires permitted animals to be slaughtered according to Islamic law.

questions.q: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed in the diet primarily for:
options: Formation of collagen and wound healing
questions.explain: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis, supporting connective tissue and wound healing.

questions.q: Most pathogenic bacteria grow best at a pH close to:
questions.explain: Most food-poisoning bacteria favour near-neutral pH, which is why acidity is used to preserve foods.

questions.q: Vitamin C is described as enhancing iron absorption because it:
options: Converts non-haem iron into the more readily absorbed ferrous form
Binds iron so it cannot be absorbed
questions.explain: Vitamin C reduces non-haem iron to the ferrous form, which is absorbed more easily.

questions.q: Basal metabolic rate (BMR) is defined as the energy needed to:
options: Maintain essential body functions at complete rest
questions.explain: BMR is the energy required to sustain basic functions such as respiration and circulation at rest.

questions.q: Irradiation as a preservation method works by:
options: Using ionising radiation to destroy micro-organisms and pests
questions.explain: Irradiation exposes food to ionising radiation, killing micro-organisms and extending shelf life.

questions.q: On a food label, the 14 major allergens (such as nuts and milk) must be:
options: Emphasised, for example in bold, within the ingredients list
questions.explain: Law requires the 14 named allergens to be emphasised in the ingredients list so consumers can identify them.

questions.q: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) extends shelf life mainly by:
options: Heating the food in the pack
Altering the gases around the food to slow spoilage
questions.explain: MAP changes the proportions of gases (e.g. reducing oxygen) to slow microbial and chemical spoilage.

questions.q: Listeria monocytogenes is of special concern because, unlike most pathogens, it can:
questions.explain: Listeria can multiply slowly at fridge temperatures, posing a risk in chilled ready-to-eat foods.

questions.q: Combining beans on toast to obtain a full set of essential amino acids is an example of:
questions.explain: Protein complementation combines two LBV foods whose limiting amino acids differ to give the full set.

questions.q: Lecithin in egg yolk acts as an emulsifier in mayonnaise because it:
options: Has one part attracted to oil and one part attracted to water
Thickens the mixture by absorbing water
Coagulates the oil into solid particles
Raises the pH of the mixture
questions.explain: An emulsifier has hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends, holding oil and water together as a stable emulsion.

questions.q: A complete protein from a single plant source that supplies all essential amino acids is:
questions.explain: Soya is unusual among plant foods in supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: In HACCP, a 'critical control point' is a step at which:
options: Control is essential to prevent or eliminate a hazard
questions.explain: A critical control point is a stage where control is essential to remove or reduce a hazard to a safe level.
